propositions: Cloud probe hardcodes RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES to ['Resolved','Done','Cancelled'] while DC reconciler reads the equivalent from config (ReconcilerConfig.resolved_statuses), creating parity gap.
A Cloud tenant with non-standard resolved-status names (e.g. 'Closed', 'Complete', "Won't Do") has issues misclassified as PRESENT_FILTERED instead of PRESENT_RESOLVED due to the hardcoded set.

JiraConfig must expose resolved_statuses as a configurable list[str] field, parsed from [tool.rebar.jira] section and overridable via REBAR_JIRA_RESOLVED_STATUSES environment variable, defaulting to the current three names.

The probe's classify_probe_response must resolve the status set from loaded config at runtime, falling back to the module-level default when the configured list is empty, unset, or malformed (ConfigError).

A tenant setting custom resolved_statuses (e.g. ['Closed','Complete']) must classify issues matching those names as PRESENT_RESOLVED and issues outside that set as PRESENT_FILTERED, while unset config preserves backward compatibility.
